extracted.intended_audience: lawyers, judges, news-agency managers, and journalists studying news-distribution rules and litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Affidavits and hearing transcript detailing The Associated Press by-laws, contractual provisions, operational time-rules, and prohibitions on disclosure — used to assess membership duties, exclusivity, and misappropriation of news in a legal dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: News service furnished only to members
rubrics_metrics.description: Article VII Sec. 4: "The news service of this Corporation shall be furnished only to members thereof, or to the newspapers represented by them and specified in their certificates of membership."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express exclusivity rule: the corporation's news may be supplied only to its members or the specific newspapers named in membership certificates. No additional examples provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use to specified newspaper/language/place
rubrics_metrics.description: Article VII Sec. 5: "A member shall publish the news of The Associated Press only in the newspaper, the language and the place specified in his certificate of membership and he shall not permit any other use to be made of the news furnished by the Corporation to him or to the newspaper which he represents."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership certificates define the sole authorized publication context (paper, language, place). This prohibits diverting AP material to other publications, languages, or territories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for receipt and publication of news
rubrics_metrics.description: Article VII Sec. 6 (time rules): "The time limits for the receipt and publication of news by members shall be (standard time...): Morning papers to receive not later than 9 a. m. and to publish not earlier than 9 p. m., except... morning papers may publish not earlier than 5 p. m. ... Sunday editions ... after 9 p. m. Saturday; afternoon papers to receive not later than 6 p. m. and to publish not earlier than 9 a. m. The service to afternoon papers between 4 p. m. and 6 p. m. to be of bulletin character; provided, that the Board of Directors may authorize that upon extraordinary occasions The Associated Press dispatches may be used in extra editions or for bulletins outside of the hours named."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies precise windows for delivery and permissible publication times (including exceptions). Also authorizes the Board to permit extraordinary departures. These provisions govern when subscribers may lawfully publish AP dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: No supplying member-furnished news to other members in same district
rubrics_metrics.description: Article VII Sec. 8: "No news furnished to the Corporation by a member shall be supplied by the Corporation to any other member publishing a newspaper within the district which the Board of Directors shall have described..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects local exclusivity: news that a member supplies to AP must not be redistributed by AP to another member who publishes in the same defined district.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on furnishing AP news in advance to non-members / improper redistribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Article VIII Sec. 6: "No member shall furnish, or permit any one in his employ or connected with the newspaper specified in his certificate of membership to furnish, to any person who is not a member, the news of the Corporation in advance of publication, or to another member any news received from the Corporation which the Corporation is itself debarred from furnishing to such member, nor conduct his business in such a manner that the news furnished by the Corporation may be communicated to any person, firm, corporation, or association not entitled to receive the same."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbids advance disclosure to non-members, forbids passing along material AP itself may not supply to a given member, and requires subscribers to organize their operations to prevent unauthorized dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on furnishing to non-members news a member must supply to AP
rubrics_metrics.description: Article VIII Sec. 7: "No member shall furnish, or permit any one to furnish, to any one not a member of this Corporation, the news which he is required by the By-Laws to supply to this Corporation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically forbids members from giving to outsiders any local or other news they are obliged to submit to AP for collective distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board resolution allowing bulletin-board displays as an exception
rubrics_metrics.description: April 21, 1913 Board resolution: "the public display of news upon bulletin boards at the main or branch offices of a newspaper in its own territory, does not constitute a violation of the By-laws which provide that no member shall furnish the news of The Associated Press in advance of publication, to any person who is not a member..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a limited, formal exception: internal/public bulletin-board display in the newspaper's own territory is not treated as impermissible advance furnishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate and assent: member use strictly limited
rubrics_metrics.description: When elected, a member receives a certificate of membership which "entitles him to the use of the news furnished by The Associated Press for publication in the newspaper specified in his certificate of membership, and for no other purpose whatsoever." Each member also signs the Charter and By-laws and assents to be bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Becoming a member requires explicit assent to restrictions; the certificate is the contractual instrument limiting permitted use of AP material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-news supply obligation and prohibition on giving it outside AP
rubrics_metrics.description: By-laws (as explained at hearing): members are required to furnish the local news of their vicinage to The Associated Press, and "the by-laws provide that the local news ... shall not be given by this member to anybody outside The Associated Press."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must provide local news to AP for collective use and must not separately distribute that local news to non-members; this protects the cooperative pool of local reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-quality desiderata: efficiency, adequacy, reliability, cheapness, exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Court/hearing statement: "The value of this news to the members of The Associated Press necessarily depends upon the efficiency with which the corporation is managed, upon the adequacy, the reliability, the cheapness of the news, and upon the fact that the news is kept exclusive for the benefit of members..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the operational/quality metrics by which the news service's value is judged; failures in these areas (e.g., loss of exclusivity) threaten the organization's viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical limit on confidentiality due to publication schedules/time zones
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing/affidavit observation: simultaneous publication nationwide is impossible because eastern papers print and distribute many hours before western papers; thus news cannot be kept confidential until all members have published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational reality modifies expectations of absolute simultaneity — by-laws/time-rules must be interpreted in light of distribution timing across different time zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual subscriber clause: news furnished for publication and no other use
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of INS–Cleveland contract: International News Service contract provides it will furnish and deliver a full-day leased wire news service "for publication by the party of the second part ... and for no other use or purpose" until specified date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical subscriber contracts explicitly limit the use of supplied news to publication in the contracting paper and prohibit other uses; such clauses are used by both AP and INS to define rights and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited acquisition methods / piracy (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation of unlawful/immoral appropriation: defendant was systematically pirating AP news by bribing member employees to supply dispatches as soon as received, then transmitting them to defendant's patrons (example: Cleveland News telegraph editor tipped INS and was paid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes concrete prohibited/evasive practices (bribery, tipping, immediate telephone transmission) that violate by-laws and contractual non-disclosure and are cited as examples of actionable misappropriation.
